```{r g10-planning-helpers}
pub_dir <- file.path('..', '..', 'data', 'quick-sim',
                     'carryover-closed-form', 'published-planning')
pub_ok <- function(f, dir = pub_dir) {
  p <- file.path(dir, f)
  m <- file.path(dir, 'PARAM_SET')
  if (file.exists(p) && file.exists(m) &&
      identical(readLines(m, n = 1L), 'published')) p else NA_character_
}
PENDING <- '\\textbf{[pending]}'
pend <- function(have, expr) if (have) expr else PENDING
## Two rates differ when they are more than two combined Monte Carlo
## SEs apart.
rate_cmp <- function(p1, n1, p0, n0) {
  se <- sqrt(p1 * (1 - p1) / n1 + p0 * (1 - p0) / n0)
  if (abs(p1 - p0) <= 2 * se) 0L else as.integer(sign(p1 - p0))
}

## 24-rho-sweep.R: separable AR(1), bound by design and half-life, and
## the E9 sample size for 80 percent power by rho.
rb_dir <- file.path('..', '..', 'data', 'quick-sim', 'carryover-closed-form',
                    'rho-stage', 'rho-sweep')
rb <- read.csv(file.path(rb_dir, 'ceilings-sep.csv'))
rb_n <- read.csv(file.path(rb_dir, 'planning-n80-by-rho.csv'))
rb_min <- function(r, th) min(rb$ceiling[rb$rho == r & rb$t_half == th])
rb_bind <- function(r, th) {
  k <- rb$rho == r & rb$t_half == th
  rb$design[k][which.min(rb$ceiling[k])]
}
rb_f <- function(v) sprintf('%.3f', v)
```

```{r planningg10data}
## Driver 19, --params published, blocks P and F (published-planning/)
## and block N (published-planning/block-N/); pub_ok(), pend() and
## rate_cmp() are defined in the fig4bg10data chunk.
pg_file <- pub_ok('planning-g10.csv')
pg9_file <- pub_ok('planning-g9.csv')
have_pg <- !is.na(pg_file) && !is.na(pg9_file)
if (have_pg) {
  pg <- read.csv(pg_file)
  pg9 <- read.csv(pg9_file)
  pg_key <- c('design', 'c_bm', 't_half', 'N_label')
  pg_vs9 <- merge(pg, pg9, by = pg_key, suffixes = c('', '_g9'))
  stopifnot(nrow(pg_vs9) == nrow(pg), nrow(pg) == nrow(pg9))
  pg_alt <- pg[pg$c_bm > 0, ]
  pg_n80 <- pg_alt[pg_alt$N_label == 'N80_E9' & !pg_alt$capped, ]
  pg_cap <- pg_alt[pg_alt$N_label == 'N80_E9' & pg_alt$capped, ]
}
pg_design <- c(Hybrid = 'Hybrid', `OL+BDC` = 'OL+BDC', Crossover = 'CO')
pg_cell <- function(d, cbm, th, nlab) {
  pg[pg$design == pg_design[d] & pg$c_bm == cbm & pg$t_half == th &
     pg$N_label == nlab, ]
}
pg_pow <- function(d, cbm, th, nlab = '70', dagger = TRUE) pend(have_pg, {
  r <- pg_cell(d, cbm, th, nlab)
  if (nrow(r) != 1) return('')
  paste0(sprintf('%.3f', r$power), if (dagger && r$capped) '$^\\dagger$' else '')
})
pg_mcse <- function(d, cbm, th, nlab = '70')
  pend(have_pg, sprintf('%.3f', pg_cell(d, cbm, th, nlab)$mcse))
fmt_range <- function(x) sprintf('%.3f to %.3f', min(x), max(x))
pg_vs9_max <- pend(have_pg,
  sprintf('%.3f', max(abs(pg_vs9$power - pg_vs9$power_g9))))
pg_size_range <- pend(have_pg, fmt_range(pg$size[!is.na(pg$size)]))
pg_size_mcse <- pend(have_pg, sprintf('%.3f', max(pg$mcse[pg$c_bm == 0])))
pg_size_reps <- pend(have_pg, format(max(pg$n_reps[pg$c_bm == 0]),
                                     big.mark = ','))
pg_alt_reps <- pend(have_pg, format(max(pg_alt$n_reps), big.mark = ','))
pg_alt_mcse <- pend(have_pg, sprintf('%.3f', max(pg_alt$mcse)))
pg_n80_range <- pend(have_pg, fmt_range(pg_n80$power))
pg_n80_n <- pend(have_pg, nrow(pg_n80))
pg_cap_range <- pend(have_pg, fmt_range(pg_cap$power))
pg_cap_n <- pend(have_pg, nrow(pg_cap))
## Uncapped cells only: a capped cell ran below the E9 sample size.
pg_min_n80 <- pend(have_pg, sprintf('%.3f', min(pg_n80$power)))
pg_nonconv_max <- pend(have_pg, sprintf('%.3f', max(pg$nonconv)))
pg_nonconv_pct <- pend(have_pg, sprintf('%.1f', 100 * max(pg$nonconv)))

## Closed-form E9 power at N = 70 (17-rho-stage.R, planning-n80.csv).
pn80 <- read.csv(file.path('..', '..', 'data', 'quick-sim',
                           'carryover-closed-form', 'rho-stage',
                           'planning-n80.csv'))
e9_pow <- function(d, cbm, th) {
  v <- pn80$power_N70[pn80$design == pg_design[[d]] & pn80$c_bm == cbm &
                      pn80$t_half == th]
  stopifnot(length(v) == 1)
  v
}
e9_fmt <- function(d, cbm, th) sprintf('%.3f', e9_pow(d, cbm, th))
## G10 at N = 70 against closed-form E9, every alternative cell: counts
## of cells where G10 is more than two Monte Carlo SEs above, within,
## and below.
pg_vs_e9 <- if (have_pg) {
  a <- pg_alt[pg_alt$N_label == '70', ]
  e9 <- mapply(function(d, cb, th) {
    e9_pow(names(pg_design)[pg_design == d], cb, th)
  }, a$design, a$c_bm, a$t_half)
  z <- (a$power - e9) / a$mcse
  c(above = sum(z > 2), within = sum(abs(z) <= 2), below = sum(z < -2),
    cells = nrow(a))
} else NULL
pg_vs_e9_txt <- pend(have_pg, {
  k <- pg_vs_e9
  if (k[['above']] == k[['cells']]) {
    sprintf('higher power than E9 in every one of the %d cells', k[['cells']])
  } else {
    cnt <- function(n) if (n == 0) 'none' else as.character(n)
    sprintf(paste('power more than two Monte Carlo SEs above that of E9 in',
                  '%d of the %d cells, within two SEs in %s and below in %s'),
            k[['above']], k[['cells']], cnt(k[['within']]),
            cnt(k[['below']]))
  }
})
## Is the closed-form E9 rule conservative for G10? At the E9 sample
## size, every uncapped cell must reach 0.80 within two Monte Carlo
## SEs.
pg_short <- if (have_pg) pg_n80[pg_n80$power < 0.8 - 2 * pg_n80$mcse, ] else NULL
pg_conservative <- have_pg && nrow(pg_short) == 0
## The text names the crossover design as the one with the smallest
## margin at the E9 sample size.
stopifnot(!have_pg ||
  names(which.min(tapply(pg_n80$power, pg_n80$design, min))) == 'CO')

## Block N: N for 80 percent power of G10 in the Hybrid design.
n80_dir <- file.path(pub_dir, 'block-N')
n80_file <- pub_ok('n80-g10.csv', n80_dir)
n80_meta_file <- pub_ok('meta.rds', n80_dir)
have_n80 <- !is.na(n80_file) && !is.na(n80_meta_file)
if (have_n80) {
  n80 <- read.csv(n80_file)
  n80_meta <- readRDS(n80_meta_file)
  n80_in <- n80[!n80$extrapolated, ]
}
n80_mult_txt <- pend(have_n80, sprintf('%g to %g',
  min(n80_meta$n80_mult), max(n80_meta$n80_mult)))
n80_k <- pend(have_n80, length(n80_meta$n80_mult))
n80_reps <- pend(have_n80, format(n80_meta$reps_n80, big.mark = ','))
n80_ratio_range <- pend(have_n80, if (nrow(n80_in) == 0) 'not estimable' else
  sprintf('%.2f to %.2f', min(n80_in$ratio_to_E9), max(n80_in$ratio_to_E9)))
n80_n_in <- pend(have_n80, nrow(n80_in))
n80_n_ex <- pend(have_n80, sum(n80$extrapolated))
```

**Sample size.** Table \@ref(tab:planning) gives the total $N$ for 80%
power under the recommended DGP, by design, $c_{bm}$ and half-life: in
closed form for the paired-difference statistic E9, and by simulation
for the recommended analysis G10 in the Hybrid design. At
the pharmacological half-life the Hybrid design needs about 280
participants at $c_{bm} = 0.25$ and 84 at 0.45. At a 1-week half-life
those rise to 480 and 146.

**The recommended analysis at the planned sample sizes.** The
companion paper [@pmsimstats-paper02] recommends the analysis G10 for
the interaction. Stage 2 introduced it as a random-intercept CAR(1)
model; its half-life selection matters here. Its drug indicator is
the exposure-decayed $D_{bc}$ at an analysis half-life chosen by AIC
over 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 weeks. The selection uses maximum-likelihood
fits of the model without the interaction, so the choice of half-life
does not depend on the term under test. The model at the chosen
half-life is refitted by REML with the interaction, and the
interaction is tested with CR2 cluster-robust standard errors and
Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. The grid of half-lives does not
include 0 or the pharmacological values of 0.1 to 0.2 week, so at
those true values G10 uses an analysis half-life of at least 0.25
week. The AIC-chosen analyses of the stress test also consider 0
(Table \@ref(tab:estimands)). We simulated G10 under the recommended
DGP with the default values in every cell of Table
\@ref(tab:planning), at $N = 70$ and at the E9 sample size for 80
percent power, with `r pg_alt_reps` replicates per cell. We also
simulated the null ($c_{bm} = 0$) at $N = 70$ for each design and
half-life with `r pg_size_reps` replicates. Table
\@ref(tab:planningg10) gives the rejection rates at the 0.2- and 1-week
half-lives. Where the E9 sample size exceeded 400, or was above 800 and
not computed, the cell ran at $N = 400$ and is marked.

Three results follow. First, G10 rejected the null at
`r pg_size_range` across the nine design-by-half-life cells, including
the half-life of 0 not shown in the table (Monte
Carlo SE at most `r pg_size_mcse`). Second, at $N = 70$ G10 has
`r pg_vs_e9_txt`. In the Hybrid design at $c_{bm} = 0.25$ and the
0.2-week half-life, G10 power is `r pg_pow('Hybrid', 0.25, 0.2)`
(MCSE `r pg_mcse('Hybrid', 0.25, 0.2)`) against
`r e9_fmt('Hybrid', 0.25, 0.2)` for E9. In the crossover design at the
same cell it is `r pg_pow('Crossover', 0.25, 0.2)` (MCSE
`r pg_mcse('Crossover', 0.25, 0.2)`) against
`r e9_fmt('Crossover', 0.25, 0.2)`. Third, at the E9 sample size for
80 percent power, G10 power is `r pg_n80_range` in the `r pg_n80_n`
uncapped cells, and `r pg_cap_range` in the `r pg_cap_n` cells that
ran at $N = 400$. `r if (!have_pg) PENDING else if (pg_conservative) paste0('Under the recommended DGP at $\\rho = 0.7$ with the default values, the closed-form E9 rule is therefore conservative for G10. A trial sized by Table \\@ref(tab:planning) and analyzed with G10 had power of at least ', pg_min_n80, ' in every uncapped cell, with the smallest margin in the crossover design.') else sprintf('The closed-form E9 rule is therefore not conservative for G10 in every cell: in %d of the %d uncapped cells G10 power at the E9 sample size is more than two Monte Carlo SEs below 0.80.', nrow(pg_short), nrow(pg_n80))`
Fits failed to converge in at most `r pg_nonconv_max` of replicates in
any cell, and the rejection rates are computed over converged fits.

The same simulated trials were also analyzed with G9, which chooses
the half-life by AIC with the interaction in the model. In every cell
the G9 and G10 rejection rates differ by at most `r pg_vs9_max`.

**The sample size for G10.** In the nine Hybrid cells we simulated G10
at `r n80_k` multiples of the E9 sample size, from `r n80_mult_txt`
times, with `r n80_reps` replicates at each. In each cell we fitted a
probit regression of rejection on $\log N$. The G10 columns of Table
\@ref(tab:planning) give the $N$ at which the fitted power is 0.80. `r if (have_n80 && sum(n80$extrapolated) == 0) paste0('That $N$ lies inside the simulated range in all ', n80_n_in, ' cells, and it is ', n80_ratio_range, ' times the E9 value.') else paste0('In the ', n80_n_in, ' cells where that $N$ lies inside the simulated range, it is ', n80_ratio_range, ' times the E9 value. In the remaining ', n80_n_ex, ' cells it lies outside the range, and the value is an extrapolation from the fitted curve and is marked.')` The E9 values are
closed form, so this comparison is the measured difference between
the paired-difference approximation and the analysis a trial would
use.

```{r planningrhodata}
## Block P at rho 0.5 and 0.9: driver 19 with --rho and --plan-file
## (athena job 19, joe job 12, commit 644f958), published-planning/
## rho<R>/; closed-form grids from 24-rho-sweep.R.
pr_rhos <- c(0.5, 0.7, 0.9)
pr_cf_dir <- file.path('..', '..', 'data', 'quick-sim',
                       'carryover-closed-form', 'rho-stage')
pr_dir <- function(r) if (r == 0.7) pub_dir else
  file.path(pub_dir, sprintf('rho%g', r))
pr_list <- lapply(pr_rhos, function(r) {
  f <- pub_ok('planning-g10.csv', pr_dir(r))
  if (is.na(f)) NULL else cbind(rho = r, read.csv(f))
})
have_pr <- !any(vapply(pr_list, is.null, logical(1)))
pr_cf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pr_rhos, function(r) {
  f <- if (r == 0.7) 'planning-n80.csv' else
    sprintf('planning-n80-rho%g.csv', r)
  d <- read.csv(file.path(pr_cf_dir, f))
  if (!'feasible' %in% names(d)) d$feasible <- TRUE
  cbind(rho = r, d[, c('design', 'c_bm', 't_half', 'N80', 'power_N70',
                       'feasible')])
}))
pr_grid <- list(`0.5` = c(0.25, 0.35, 0.45), `0.7` = c(0.25, 0.35, 0.45),
                `0.9` = c(0.20, 0.25, 0.30))
if (have_pr) {
  pr <- do.call(rbind, pr_list)
  pr_new <- pr[pr$rho != 0.7, ]
  pr_null <- pr_new[pr_new$c_bm == 0, ]
  pr_n80 <- pr_new[pr_new$c_bm > 0 & pr_new$N_label == 'N80_E9' &
                   !pr_new$capped, ]
  ## Every feasible closed-form cell was simulated at both sample sizes.
  stopifnot(nrow(pr_new[pr_new$c_bm > 0, ]) ==
              2 * sum(pr_cf$feasible[pr_cf$rho != 0.7]))
  co9 <- pr_new$rho == 0.9 & pr_new$design == 'CO'
  pr_fail_co9 <- pr_new$nonconv[co9 & pr_new$N_label == '70']
  pr_fail_co9_n80 <- pr_new$nonconv[co9 & pr_new$N_label == 'N80_E9' &
                                    !pr_new$capped]
  pr_fail_co9_cap <- pr_new$nonconv[co9 & pr_new$capped]
  pr_fail_other <- pr_new$nonconv[!co9]
}
pr_cell <- function(r, d, cb, th, nlab) {
  pr[pr$rho == r & pr$design == d & abs(pr$c_bm - cb) < 1e-9 &
     pr$t_half == th & pr$N_label == nlab, ]
}
pr_e9n <- function(r, d, cb, th = 0.2) {
  k <- pr_cf$rho == r & pr_cf$design == d & abs(pr_cf$c_bm - cb) < 1e-9 &
    pr_cf$t_half == th
  stopifnot(sum(k) == 1)
  if (!pr_cf$feasible[k]) NA_integer_ else pr_cf$N80[k]
}
pr_rng <- function(x, d = 3) sprintf(paste0('%.', d, 'f to %.', d, 'f'),
                                     min(x), max(x))
pr_pct <- function(x) sprintf('%.0f', 100 * x)
pr_size_txt <- pend(have_pr, pr_rng(pr_null$size))
pr_n80_txt <- function(r) pend(have_pr, pr_rng(pr_n80$power[pr_n80$rho == r]))
pr_g <- function(r, d, cb, th, nlab) pend(have_pr,
  sprintf('%.3f', pr_cell(r, d, cb, th, nlab)$power))
pr_fail_txt <- pend(have_pr, paste(pr_pct(min(pr_fail_co9)), 'to',
                                   pr_pct(max(pr_fail_co9))))
pr_fail_n80_txt <- pend(have_pr, paste(pr_pct(min(pr_fail_co9_n80)), 'to',
                                       pr_pct(max(pr_fail_co9_n80))))
pr_fail_cap_txt <- pend(have_pr, sprintf('%.1f',
                                         100 * max(pr_fail_co9_cap)))
pr_fail_other_txt <- pend(have_pr, sprintf('%.1f',
                                           100 * max(pr_fail_other)))
pr_ratio <- function(r) sprintf('%.1f',
  pr_e9n(r, 'CO', 0.25) / pr_e9n(r, 'Hybrid', 0.25))
## Block N at rho 0.5 and 0.9 (julia job 3, joe job 13, commit
## 4f5b789): G10 sample size for 80 percent power, Hybrid design.
n80_rho <- lapply(c(0.5, 0.9), function(r) {
  f <- pub_ok('n80-g10.csv', file.path(pr_dir(r), 'block-N'))
  if (is.na(f)) NULL else cbind(rho = r, read.csv(f))
})
have_n80r <- have_n80 && !any(vapply(n80_rho, is.null, logical(1)))
n80r_in <- function(r) {
  d <- n80_rho[[match(r, c(0.5, 0.9))]]
  d[!d$extrapolated & !is.na(d$N80_G), ]
}
n80r_ratio <- function(r) pend(have_n80r, {
  d <- n80r_in(r)
  sprintf('%.2f to %.2f', min(d$ratio_to_E9), max(d$ratio_to_E9))
})
n80r_ex <- pend(have_n80r, sum(vapply(n80_rho, function(d)
  sum(d$extrapolated | is.na(d$N80_G)), numeric(1))))
## The text states that G10 power at the E9 sample size exceeds 0.80 in
## every uncapped cell at both new values of rho, and that the
## crossover failures at 0.9 are the only ones above 3 percent.
stopifnot(!have_pr || (all(pr_n80$power > 0.8) &&
                       max(pr_fail_other) < 0.03 && min(pr_fail_co9) > 0.03 &&
                       min(pr_fail_co9_n80) > 0.03 &&
                       max(pr_fail_co9_cap) < 0.01))
## Typed in the Abstract and Limitations: bound 0.34 at rho 0.9, and
## about half the Hybrid sample of rho 0.7.
stopifnot(abs(rb_min(0.9, 0) - 0.34) < 0.005,
          abs(pr_e9n(0.9, 'Hybrid', 0.25) / pr_e9n(0.7, 'Hybrid', 0.25) -
                0.5) < 0.1)
```

**Serial correlation.** The planning results above assume
$\rho = 0.7$, a convention (Stage 4). We repeated the closed-form
calculation and the G10 simulation at $\rho = 0.5$ and 0.9, with the
same seeds and replicate counts. At 0.5 the grid of $c_{bm}$ is
unchanged, and one cell lies above its bound (OL+BDC at 0.45 without
carryover). At 0.9 the Hybrid bound falls to `r rb_f(rb_min(0.9, 0))`,
so the grid moves to 0.20, 0.25 and 0.30. Table
\@ref(tab:planningrho) gives the cells at the 0.2-week half-life.
Below, ranges over all half-lives cover 0, 0.2 and 1 week.

In the Hybrid design the required sample size depends strongly on
$\rho$ above 0.7 and little below it. At $c_{bm} = 0.25$ the E9 rule
gives `r pr_e9n(0.5, 'Hybrid', 0.25)`, `r pr_e9n(0.7, 'Hybrid', 0.25)`
and `r pr_e9n(0.9, 'Hybrid', 0.25)` participants at $\rho = 0.5$, 0.7
and 0.9. The crossover needs `r pr_ratio(0.7)` times the Hybrid sample
at 0.7 and `r pr_ratio(0.9)` times at 0.9. The likely reason is visit
spacing. The Hybrid design compares on- and off-drug visits one week
apart, where a high serial correlation cancels most of the shared
noise. The crossover compares two blocks of four visits 2.5 weeks
apart, ten weeks apart on average. G10 rejected
the null at `r pr_size_txt` in the 18 design-by-half-life cells at the
two new values. At the E9 sample size its power was
`r pr_n80_txt(0.5)` at $\rho = 0.5$ and `r pr_n80_txt(0.9)` at 0.9, in
the uncapped cells. The E9 rule therefore stays conservative for G10,
and at $\rho = 0.9$ it is very conservative. There G10 had power
`r pr_g(0.9, 'Hybrid', 0.25, 0.2, '70')` in the Hybrid design at
$c_{bm} = 0.25$ with only 70 participants. We repeated the G10
sample-size search in the Hybrid design (Table
\@ref(tab:planningrho)). Over all three half-lives it gives `r n80r_ratio(0.5)` times the E9 value at $\rho = 0.5$ and
`r n80r_ratio(0.9)` times at 0.9, against `r n80_ratio_range` at 0.7.
`r if (identical(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(n80r_ex)), 0)) 'At both new values the sample size lies inside the simulated range in every cell.' else paste0('Cells whose value lies outside the simulated range are left out of these ranges: ', n80r_ex, ' at the two new values.')`

In the crossover design at $\rho = 0.9$, `r pr_fail_txt` percent of G10
fits failed in each cell at $N = 70$, and `r pr_fail_n80_txt` percent
at the E9 sample sizes below 400. In the cells that ran at $N = 400$
at most `r pr_fail_cap_txt` percent failed. In every other cell at the
two new values at most `r pr_fail_other_txt` percent failed. In the failed replicates we
refitted, the model chosen by AIC put the serial correlation at its
upper limit of 1 and the random-intercept SD near zero. A correlation
that does not decay cannot be told apart from a random intercept, and
the CR2 step then failed because the fitted covariance was singular.
The rates in Table \@ref(tab:planningrho) are over the fits that
succeeded. A trialist who expects slow decay and plans a crossover
analyzed with G10 should expect such failures and specify a fallback
model in advance.

**When these sample sizes apply.** The sample sizes assume, as the
whole paper does, that the biomarker is not prognostic (Aims). G10
does not hold its level under every prognostic pathway. A trial in
which such a pathway is plausible should be planned for an analysis
that does, and its sample size is larger; the companion paper gives
both [@pmsimstats-paper15].

```{r planning}
## E9 (closed form) for every design; G10 (block N, rho = 0.7) for the
## Hybrid design only, the design in which it was searched for.
tab <- data.frame(
  design = c('Hybrid', '', '', 'OL+BDC', '', '', 'Crossover', '', ''),
  cbm = rep(c(0.25, 0.35, 0.45), 3),
  slope = rep(c(2.0, 2.8, 3.6), 3))
pn80 <- read.csv(file.path('..', '..', 'data', 'quick-sim',
                           'carryover-closed-form', 'rho-stage',
                           'planning-n80.csv'))
pn80_get <- function(col, th) {
  d <- rep(c('Hybrid', 'OL+BDC', 'CO'), each = 3)
  mapply(function(dd, cb) {
    v <- pn80[[col]][pn80$design == dd & pn80$c_bm == cb & pn80$t_half == th]
    stopifnot(length(v) == 1)
    v
  }, d, tab$cbm, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}
pn80_n <- function(th) {
  v <- pn80_get('N80', th)
  ifelse(is.na(v), '> 800', as.character(v))
}
## Without carryover the E9 sample size is within a few percent of its
## 0.2-week value, so the 0-week column is not shown.
pn80_d0 <- {
  a <- pn80_get('N80', 0); b <- pn80_get('N80', 0.2)
  max(abs(b - a) / b, na.rm = TRUE)
}
stopifnot(pn80_d0 < 0.05)
g10n <- function(cb, th) {
  if (!have_n80) return(PENDING)
  r <- n80[abs(n80$c_bm - cb) < 1e-9 & n80$t_half == th, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  paste0(if (is.na(r$N80_G)) 'n/e' else ceiling(r$N80_G),
         if (r$extrapolated) '$^\\ddagger$' else '')
}
tab$n02 <- pn80_n(0.2)
tab$n1 <- pn80_n(1)
tab$g02 <- c(vapply(c(0.25, 0.35, 0.45), g10n, '', th = 0.2), rep('', 6))
tab$g1 <- c(vapply(c(0.25, 0.35, 0.45), g10n, '', th = 1), rep('', 6))
knitr::kable(tab, booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3, escape = FALSE, align = 'lrrrrrr',
  linesep = '',
  col.names = c('Design', '$c_{bm}$', 'Slope (points per SD)',
                '0.2 week', '1 week', '0.2 week', '1 week'),
  caption = paste0('Total $N$ for 80 percent power at $\\alpha = 0.05$ under the recommended DGP (separable AR(1), $\\rho = 0.7$, $c_1 = 0.2$, decaying biomarker-response correlation, carryover decaying from the last on-drug mean, default values), by design, interaction strength and carryover half-life, with the implied slope in symptom points per SD of biomarker ($\\sigma_{BR} = 8$). E9: closed form. G10: Hybrid design only; the $N$ at which a probit regression of rejection on $\\log N$, fitted to simulations at ', n80_k, ' multiples of the E9 value (', n80_reps, ' replicates each), reaches 0.80, rounded up. Without carryover the E9 values are at most ', sprintf('%.0f', 100 * pn80_d0), ' percent below those at 0.2 week. Participants are allocated to paths in fixed proportions (18, 18, 17, 17 in the Hybrid design at $N = 70$).', if (have_n80 && any(n80$extrapolated)) ' $\\ddagger$: outside the simulated range of $N$, an extrapolation.' else '')) |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(' ' = 3, 'E9 (closed form)' = 2, 'G10 (simulated)' = 2), escape = FALSE)
```

```{r planningg10}
th <- c(0.2, 1)
des <- c('Hybrid', 'OL+BDC', 'Crossover')
rows <- expand.grid(cbm = c(0, 0.25, 0.35, 0.45), design = des,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[, c('design', 'cbm')]
cell_or_blank <- function(d, cb, t, nlab) {
  if (cb == 0 && nlab == 'N80_E9') return('')
  pg_pow(d, cb, t, nlab)
}
tab9 <- data.frame(
  design = ifelse(rows$cbm == 0, rows$design, ''),
  cbm = sprintf('%.2f', rows$cbm),
  p70_02 = mapply(cell_or_blank, rows$design, rows$cbm, 0.2, '70'),
  p70_1 = mapply(cell_or_blank, rows$design, rows$cbm, 1, '70'),
  p80_02 = mapply(cell_or_blank, rows$design, rows$cbm, 0.2, 'N80_E9'),
  p80_1 = mapply(cell_or_blank, rows$design, rows$cbm, 1, 'N80_E9'))
knitr::kable(tab9, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, align = 'lrrrrr',
  linesep = '', row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c('Design', '$c_{bm}$', '0.2 week', '1 week',
                '0.2 week', '1 week'),
  caption = paste0('Rejection rate of the analysis G10 under the recommended DGP of Table \\ref{tab:planning}, by design, interaction strength and carryover half-life, at $N = 70$ and at the closed-form E9 $N$ for 80 percent power. Rows with $c_{bm} = 0$ give the size at $N = 70$ (', pg_size_reps, ' replicates per cell, Monte Carlo SE at most ', pg_size_mcse, '); the other rows give power (', pg_alt_reps, ' replicates per cell, Monte Carlo SE at most ', pg_alt_mcse, '). $\\dagger$: the E9 sample size exceeds 400 and the cell ran at $N = 400$. Rejection rates are over converged fits (at most ', pg_nonconv_pct, ' percent of replicates failed in any cell).')) |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(' ' = 2, 'At $N = 70$' = 2, 'At the E9 $N$' = 2), escape = FALSE)
```

```{r planningrho}
pr_new_rhos <- c(0.5, 0.9)
pr_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pr_new_rhos, function(r)
  expand.grid(cbm = pr_grid[[as.character(r)]],
              design = c('Hybrid', 'OL+BDC', 'CO'), rho = r,
              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
pr_txt <- function(r, d, cb, nlab) {
  if (!have_pr) return(PENDING)
  x <- pr_cell(r, d, cb, 0.2, nlab)
  if (nrow(x) == 0) return('')
  paste0(sprintf('%.3f', x$power), if (x$capped) '$^\\dagger$' else '')
}
pr_g10n <- function(r, d, cb) {
  if (d != 'Hybrid') return('')
  if (!have_n80r) return(PENDING)
  x <- n80_rho[[match(r, c(0.5, 0.9))]]
  x <- x[abs(x$c_bm - cb) < 1e-9 & x$t_half == 0.2, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(x) == 1)
  paste0(if (is.na(x$N80_G)) 'n/e' else ceiling(x$N80_G),
         if (x$extrapolated) '$^\\ddagger$' else '')
}
tabr <- data.frame(
  rho = ifelse(!duplicated(pr_rows$rho), sprintf('%.1f', pr_rows$rho), ''),
  design = ifelse(!duplicated(pr_rows[, c('rho', 'design')]),
                  ifelse(pr_rows$design == 'CO', 'Crossover',
                         pr_rows$design), ''),
  cbm = sprintf('%.2f', pr_rows$cbm),
  n = mapply(function(r, d, cb) {
    v <- pr_e9n(r, d, cb)
    k <- pr_cf$rho == r & pr_cf$design == d &
      abs(pr_cf$c_bm - cb) < 1e-9 & pr_cf$t_half == 0.2
    if (!pr_cf$feasible[k]) 'not feasible' else
      if (is.na(v)) '> 800' else as.character(v)
  }, pr_rows$rho, pr_rows$design, pr_rows$cbm),
  g10n = mapply(pr_g10n, pr_rows$rho, pr_rows$design, pr_rows$cbm),
  g80 = mapply(pr_txt, pr_rows$rho, pr_rows$design, pr_rows$cbm,
               'N80_E9'),
  fail = mapply(function(r, d, cb) {
    if (!have_pr) return('')
    x <- pr_cell(r, d, cb, 0.2, '70')
    if (nrow(x) == 0) '' else pr_pct(x$nonconv)
  }, pr_rows$rho, pr_rows$design, pr_rows$cbm))
knitr::kable(tabr, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, align = 'llrrrrr',
  linesep = '', row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c('$\\rho$', 'Design', '$c_{bm}$', 'E9 $N$', 'G10 $N$',
                'G10 power at the E9 $N$', 'G10 failed (\\%)'),
  caption = paste0('Planning by serial correlation at the 0.2-week half-life, as Table \\ref{tab:planning} (which gives $\\rho = 0.7$) but at $\\rho = 0.5$ and 0.9: the closed-form total $N$ for 80 percent power of E9, the G10 $N$ for 80 percent power (Hybrid design only), G10 power at the E9 $N$ (', pend(have_pr, format(max(pr$n_reps[pr$c_bm > 0]), big.mark = ',')), ' replicates per cell), and the percent of G10 fits that failed at $N = 70$. At $\\rho = 0.9$ the grid of $c_{bm}$ lies inside the lower bound. Not feasible: $c_{bm}$ lies above the bound of that design. $\\dagger$: the E9 sample size exceeds 400 and the cell ran at $N = 400$. Power is over the fits that succeeded.')) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)
```
